ap_chemistry-f01.title: Intermolecular forces and boiling points of alkanes, an ether and an alcohol

stimulus.description: Molar masses and normal boiling points of four organic compounds

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Using the table, compare the boiling points of propane and butane, and explain the difference in terms of intermolecular forces.
parts.model_answer: Butane has the higher boiling point (273 K versus 231 K); both are nonpolar, and the larger electron cloud of butane is more polarizable, so its London dispersion forces are stronger and more energy is needed to separate the molecules.

rubric_rows.criterion: States that butane (273 K) has a higher boiling point than propane (231 K)
common_errors: says propane has the higher boiling point because it is smaller

rubric_rows.criterion: Explains that the larger, more polarizable electron cloud of butane gives stronger London dispersion forces
common_errors: says the C–C bonds of butane are stronger so they break less easily

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Draw a diagram of two ethanol molecules that shows one hydrogen bond between them. Label the hydrogen bond with a dashed line and show the atoms involved.
parts.model_answer: The hydrogen atom of the O–H group in one ethanol molecule is joined by a dashed line to the oxygen atom of the other molecule.

rubric_rows.criterion: Draws a dashed line between the hydrogen of the O–H group of one molecule and the oxygen of the second molecule
common_errors: draws the dashed line between two carbon atoms or between two hydrogen atoms

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Ethanol and dimethyl ether have the same molar mass, but ethanol has a much higher boiling point. Explain this difference in terms of intermolecular forces.
parts.model_answer: Ethanol molecules can form hydrogen bonds with one another (H bonded to O), which are stronger than the dipole–dipole forces between dimethyl ether molecules, which have no O–H group.

rubric_rows.criterion: Explains that ethanol forms hydrogen bonds, which are stronger than the forces between dimethyl ether molecules
common_errors: says the O–H bond of ethanol breaks when the liquid boils

ap_chemistry-f02.title: Types of solids and their properties

stimulus.description: A student compares two solids at 25 °C, Ag and MgO. Ag is a metallic solid, and MgO is an ionic solid.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Describe the species that make up solid MgO and the type of attraction that holds them in place.
parts.model_answer: Solid MgO contains positive and negative ions held in a lattice by electrostatic attractions.

rubric_rows.criterion: Describes positive and negative ions held in a lattice by electrostatic attractions
common_errors: describes discrete molecules held by weak dispersion forces

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Compare the electrical conductivity of solid Ag and solid MgO at 25 °C, and explain the difference in terms of the charged species that can or cannot move.
parts.model_answer: Solid Ag conducts electricity and solid MgO does not: the delocalized electrons of the metal are free to move, but in solid MgO the ions are fixed in the lattice and cannot move through the solid.

rubric_rows.criterion: States that solid Ag conducts electricity and solid MgO does not
common_errors: says both solids conduct because they contain charged species

rubric_rows.criterion: Explains with mobile delocalized electrons in Ag and fixed ions in MgO
common_errors: explains with the molar mass of the solids

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Predict which of the two solids has the higher melting point, and justify your prediction in terms of the bonding.
parts.model_answer: MgO has the higher melting point: strong electrostatic attractions between ions must be overcome. (Metals such as Cu, Fe and Ag melt at lower temperatures than these solids.)

rubric_rows.criterion: Predicts that MgO has the higher melting point and links it to the strength of the bonding throughout the solid
common_errors: says melting a network solid only separates molecules

ap_chemistry-f02.title: Types of solids and their properties

stimulus.description: A student compares two solids at 25 °C, Fe and SiC. Fe is a metallic solid, and SiC is a covalent network solid.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Describe the species that make up solid SiC and the type of attraction that holds them in place.
parts.model_answer: Solid SiC contains atoms linked by covalent bonds throughout the whole solid.

rubric_rows.criterion: Describes atoms linked by covalent bonds throughout the whole solid
common_errors: describes discrete molecules held by weak dispersion forces

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Compare the electrical conductivity of solid Fe and solid SiC at 25 °C, and explain the difference in terms of the charged species that can or cannot move.
parts.model_answer: Solid Fe conducts electricity and solid SiC does not: the delocalized electrons of the metal are free to move, but in solid SiC the electrons are localized in covalent bonds and cannot move through the solid.

rubric_rows.criterion: States that solid Fe conducts electricity and solid SiC does not
common_errors: says both solids conduct because they contain charged species

rubric_rows.criterion: Explains with mobile delocalized electrons in Fe and localized shared electrons in SiC
common_errors: explains with the molar mass of the solids

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Predict which of the two solids has the higher melting point, and justify your prediction in terms of the bonding.
parts.model_answer: SiC has the higher melting point: strong covalent bonds throughout the network must be broken. (Metals such as Cu, Fe and Ag melt at lower temperatures than these solids.)

rubric_rows.criterion: Predicts that SiC has the higher melting point and links it to the strength of the bonding throughout the solid
common_errors: says melting a network solid only separates molecules
